messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: KV cache memory pressure exceeded 90% on pool=dedicated-us-west-2-1. Autoscaler triggered paging. Suspected regression after deploy rdl-quant-122. Runbook: https://intra.redwood/runbooks/kv-cache-paging

sasha (eng-sre): seeing the alert, taking lead. can folks share immediate impact numbers? if this is a quant path regression we should consider disabling continuous batching first.

maria (eng-runtime): quick dump from metrics snapshot (past 10m):
```
kv_cache_used_bytes: 11234567890
kv_cache_capacity_bytes: 12000000000
kv_cache_evictions_rate{pool="dedicated-us-west-2-1"}: 324/s
continuous_batch_queue_depth: 48
avg_batch_size: 16 -> jumped from baseline 4
```
Top offending model variants by induced KV size: gpt6b-awq-int8@v2, gpt6b-gptq64@v3. Memory per-kv approx: awq-int8 ~ 8.6MB/kv, gptq64 ~ 4.1MB/kv (validated on node 03-07).

andre (eng-ml): this looks like the AWQ int8 kernel is selecting a dense-kv-layout path accidentally (kernel selector fallback). AWQ quantized weights should be smaller but we have a mismatch where the runtime picks the int8->fp16 fallback kernel for KV codec, which inflates per-kv size. I ran a local reproducer earlier this week (different env) and noted a similar spike when kernel_probe order changed.

kevin (support): we have 2 paid customers reporting elevated 5xx and timeouts on chat endpoints in us-west. Support ticket IDs: SUP-7891, SUP-7892. Both are pinned to dedicated-us-west-2-1. Could be partial availability.

ton y (oncall): taking action: first mitigation = disable continuous batching for the affected pool to stop KV amplification and reduce queue buildup. applying patch now.

maria (eng-runtime): proposed hotfix to pool config:
```
PATCH /api/v1/pools/dedicated-us-west-2-1/config
{
  "continuous_batching": false,
  "max_batch_size": 8,
  "kv_cache_capacity_bytes": 10000000000
}
```
Applying with 2-minute rolling across nodes to avoid warm-up storms.

andre (eng-ml): :+1: also suggest forcing kernel selection to the stable awq-quant-kernel v1.9 on that pool while we triage. Kernel pin command: `runtimectl set-kernel --pool dedicated-us-west-2-1 --model gpt6b-awq-int8 --kernel awq-1.9`

sasha (eng-sre): maria — do the autoscaler/paging logs show which nodes started paging? I want to isolate any nodes with early KV blowups to avoid noisy MIGRATE churn.

maria (eng-runtime): logs show paging started on node ids node-03-07 -> node-03-09 between 21:11:30Z and 21:14:02Z. Eviction burst coincides with a spike in avg_batch_size from 4->16. PIDs and short debug excerpt:
```
[21:14:01Z] node-03-07 runtime: kv_cache_new_entry(model=gpt6b-awq-int8, key=tok:18324) size=8624320 bytes
[21:14:01Z] node-03-07 runtime: kv_cache_entry_reused -> true
[21:14:02Z] node-03-07 runtime: eviction triggered, freed 235MB
[21:14:05Z] node-03-08 runtime: fallback kernel selected: int8->fp16_fallback (unexpected)
```

tony (oncall): hotfix applied: continuous batching disabled, max_batch_size set to 8, kernel pinned on pool to awq-1.9. Watching metrics now. Notifying support to update customers.

incident-bot: Incident status changed -> acknowledged by sasha (eng-sre). Severity: P2. Incident channel: #incidents. Updated runbook state: mitigation_in_progress.

kevin (support): letting SUP-7891/7892 know we applied mitigations; asked customers to retry. One customer reported partial recovery after 90s, another still seeing 503s.

andre (eng-ml): quick note on root cause hypothesis: kernel-probe reordering after rdl-quant-122 changed the preferred kernel candidate list. Because of that, AWQ int8 model ended up using a fallback path that writes an expanded KV layout (dense int8->fp16 conversion), increasing KV memory by ~2x. Combined with continuous batching burst this amplified into paging.

sasha (eng-sre): current numbers (2m after mitigation):
```
kv_cache_used_bytes: 82%
evictions_rate: 24/s
avg_batch_size: 5
queue_depth: 12
```
Looks much improved. Customer 1 back to normal, customer 2 reports intermittent but improving.

maria (eng-runtime): scheduled follow-ups:
- revert kernel-probe reordering in next canary and add unit test for kernel selection rank.
- add threshold alert for per-kv size delta > 30% across releases.
- add automatic circuit-breaker: if per-kv median jumps > 2x, auto-disable continuous batching for the pool and page SRE.

I filed internal ticket OP-4563 for follow-up.

andre (eng-ml): also will add a micro-test that runs kernel selection on a small sample and verifies KV footprint against a golden vector. Will PR today.

kevin (support): updating the two customers: both acknowledged; one requested postmortem and timeline. I told them we'll follow up after full RCA.

tony (oncall): handing off to sasha for postmortem and next steps. I'll monitor for the next hour then stand down.

sasha (eng-sre): thanks tony. I'll keep the incident open and collect logs/traces for the RCA. Initial severity reduced to P3. Add folks to the follow-up: @andre, @maria, @tony, @kevin.

incident-bot: Incident annotated: mitigation_action=disabled_continuous_batching,kernel_pin=awq-1.9,patch_id=rdl-hotfix-331.

sasha (eng-sre): action items captured: [OP-4563] kernel-selection test + alerting; [OP-4564] automatic continuous-batching circuit-breaker; [DOC-122] runbook update with quant-path checklist. Will post the postmortem draft in #postmortems in 48h.

kevin (support): :thumbsup: will collect customer impact details for postmortem.

maria (eng-runtime): closing note: if we re-enable continuous batching later, do it with slow ramp (batch scaling=gradual, reserve 20% extra capacity) to avoid repeated flameouts.

sasha (eng-sre): closing loop for now. incident thread will stay pinned until RCA complete. Thanks all for the quick coordination. :raised_hands:
